newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ANOTHER ROUND-THE-WORLD COMPETITOR LOST
Australian Maritime authorities have confirmed reports that another competitor in the round-the-world yacht race has lost contact with race organisers.
French Television reported that the vessel, "Groupe LG2", was half way between New Zealand and Chile when contact was lost.
DINELLI WANTS TO DESIGN SAFER YACHT
French yachtsman, Raphael Dinelli, rescued from the Southern Ocean after 22 hours on the hull of his upturned yacht, plans to turn his misfortune into a design for a safer life raft and boat.
The sailor says he'll work on the project with his rescuer, and fellow competitor in the Vendee Globe round-the-world yacht race, Peter Goss.
Mr Dinelli says he wants to design a yacht that's easier to right when it turns over.
He says he'll do that after he has a holiday and repays his debts in France, by joining Peter Goss in England.
GLAMOUR OF RACING DOESN'T EXTEND TO JOCKEYS
A lawyer representing the National Jockeys Council in the jockey pay dispute says the glamorous side of racing doesn't extend as far as the pay packets of jockey.
Anthony Gow-Gates says only about six per cent of jockeys would earn a very good living out of racing.
Jockeys took national strike action on Saturday, to try to obtain a pay increase from 70-dollars to 130-dollars a race.
Yesterday owners and trainers decided to ban jockeys for a month and use apprentices, saying jockeys have had it too good for too long.
Mr Gow-Gates says he's dismayed by the decision.
RESCUE DUE TO BEGIN THIS MORNING
A Navy helicopter will this morning attempt to pluck lone French yachtsman Thierry Dubois from the Southern Ocean, after he spent four nights in a liferaft waiting for rescue.
Dubois was competing in a solo around the world race when his yacht overturned in heavy seas on Sunday.
HMAS Adelaide intends sending its Seahawke helicopter at first light after it was unable to take off during the night because of icy conditions.
If that rescue fails Dubois will be picked up when the Adelaide reaches the area about four hours later.
Captain Raydon Gates says his crew has never attempted such a rescue.
The Adelaide will continue on to the upturned yach of Briton, Tony Bullimore.
Its hoped he is still inside the hull, but sonar devices dropped from an airforce Orion yesterday didn't detect any sign of life.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
